name: Giblet Soup
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: Giblets of four chickens or two turkeys
ingredients.originalText: Giblets of four chickens or two turkeys

ingredients.name: Three quarts of water or stock in part or any chicken bones
ingredients.originalText: Three quarts of water or stock in part or any chicken bones
ingredients.quantityText: Three quarts of water or stock in part or any chicken bones

instructions.text: Heat butter size of an egg in stew-pan, throw in the sliced onion
Add the minced carrot and turnip; when tender and a light brown, add the giblets, stirring in a tablespoonful of flour
Be careful to stir often that they do not burn
Cut up giblets and put with vegetables into soup kettle with tablespoonful of salt, teaspoonful of pepper and three quarts of water, or stock in part, if you have it, or any chicken bones
Let this simmer slowly for three hours or more; then strain it
Take all the livers, mash into them a tablespoonful of melted butter, tablespoonful browned flour; squeeze the juice of small lemon into this and add to the soup
Place in tureen yolks of three hard-boiled eggs cut in half-dozen pieces, pour over the soup; serve

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Heat butter size of an egg in stew-pan, throw in the sliced onion
2. Add the minced carrot and turnip; when tender and a light brown, add the giblets, stirring in a tablespoonful of flour
3. Be careful to stir often that they do not burn
4. Cut up giblets and put with vegetables into soup kettle with tablespoonful of salt, teaspoonful of pepper and three quarts of water, or stock in part, if you have it, or any chicken bones
5. Let this simmer slowly for three hours or more; then strain it
6. Take all the livers, mash into them a tablespoonful of melted butter, tablespoonful browned flour; squeeze the juice of small lemon into this and add to the soup
7. Place in tureen yolks of three hard-boiled eggs cut in half-dozen pieces, pour over the soup; serve
